# Music genre

Music genre

Classification of music by tradition or style

A **music genre** is a conventional category that identifies some pieces of [music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music "Music") as belonging to a shared tradition or set of conventions.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-1) [Genre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genre "Genre") is to be distinguished from [musical form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_form "Musical form") and **musical style**, although in practice these terms are sometimes used interchangeably.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-2)

Music can be divided into genres in numerous ways, sometimes broadly and with polarity, e.g., [popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music") as opposed to [art music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_music "Art music") or [folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"), or, as another example, [religious music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_music "Religious music") and [secular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secular_music "Secular music"). Often, however, classification draws on the proliferation of derivative subgenres, fusion genres, and [microgenres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microgenre "Microgenre") that has started to accrue, e.g., [screamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screamo "Screamo"), [country pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_pop "Country pop"), and [mumble rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumble_rap "Mumble rap"), respectively. The artistic nature of music means that these classifications are often subjective and controversial, and some may overlap. As genres evolve, novel music is sometimes lumped into existing categories.

## Definitions

Douglass M. Green distinguishes between genre and [form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_form "Musical form") in his 1965 book _Form in Tonal Music_. He lists [madrigal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrigal_(music) "Madrigal (music)"), [motet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motet "Motet"), [canzona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canzona "Canzona"), [ricercar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricercar "Ricercar"), and dance as examples of genres from the [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_music "Renaissance music") period. To further clarify the meaning of _genre_, Green writes about " [Beethoven's Op. 61](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violin_Concerto_(Beethoven) "Violin Concerto (Beethoven)")" and "Mendelssohn's Op. 64 ". He explains that both are identical in genre and are [violin concertos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violin_concerto "Violin concerto") that have different forms. However, Mozart's Rondo for Piano, K. 511, and the _Agnus Dei_ from his Mass, K. 317, are quite different in genre but happen to be similar in form."[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-3)

In 1982, [Franco Fabbri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Fabbri "Franco Fabbri") proposed a definition of the musical genre that is now considered to be normative:[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Moore-4) "musical genre is a set of musical events (real or possible) whose course is governed by a definite set of socially accepted rules", where a musical event can be defined as "any type of activity performed around any type of event involving sound".[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-:2-5)

A music genre or subgenre may be defined by the [musical techniques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_technique "Musical technique"), the cultural context, and the content and spirit of the themes. Geographical origin is sometimes used to identify a music genre, though a single geographical category will often include a wide variety of subgenres. Timothy Laurie argues that, since the early 1980s, "genre has graduated from being a subset of popular music studies to being an almost ubiquitous framework for constituting and evaluating musical research objects".[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-6)

The term _genre_ is generally defined similarly by many authors and musicologists, while the related term _style_ has different interpretations and definitions. Some, like [Peter van der Merwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_van_der_Merwe_(musicologist) "Peter van der Merwe (musicologist)"), treat the terms _genre_ and _style_ as the same, saying that _genre_ should be defined as pieces of music that share a certain style or "basic musical language".[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Pete-7) Others, such as Allan F. Moore, state that _genre_ and _style_ are two separate terms, and that secondary characteristics such as subject matter can also differentiate between genres.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Moore-4)

### Subtypes

"Fusion genre" redirects here. For fusion genres in literary and film works, see [Hybrid genre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_genre "Hybrid genre").

See also: [Category:Fusion music genres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Fusion_music_genres "Category:Fusion music genres")

A _[subgenre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subgenre "Subgenre")_ is a [subordinate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hierarchy "Hierarchy") within a genre.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-9) In music terms, it is a subcategory of a musical genre that adopts its basic characteristics, but also has its own set of characteristics that clearly distinguish and set it apart within the genre. A subgenre is also sometimes referred to as a style within the genre.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-12) The proliferation of popular music in the 20th century has led to over 1,200 definable subgenres of music.

A musical composition may be situated in the intersection of two or more genres, sharing characteristics of each [parent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superior_(hierarchy) "Superior (hierarchy)") genre, and therefore belong to each of them at the same time.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-:2-5) Such subgenres are known as _fusion genres_.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Examples of fusion genres include [jazz fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_fusion "Jazz fusion"), which is a fusion of [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") and rock music, and [country rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_rock "Country rock") which is a fusion of [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") and rock music.

A _[microgenre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microgenre "Microgenre")_ is a niche genre,[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-13) as well as a subcategory within major genres or their subgenres.

## Categorization and emergence of new genres

The [genealogy of musical genres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogy_of_musical_genres "Genealogy of musical genres") expresses, often in the form of a written chart. New genres of music can arise through the development of new styles of music; in addition to simply creating a new categorization. Although it is conceivable to create a musical style with no relation to existing genres, new styles usually appear under the influence of pre-existing genres.

Musicologists have sometimes classified music according to a trichotomous distinction such as Philip Tagg's "axiomatic triangle consisting of 'folk', 'art' and 'popular' musics".[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Analysing_Popular_Music_1982,_p._41-14) He explains that each of these three is distinguishable from the others according to certain criteria.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Analysing_Popular_Music_1982,_p._41-14) Tagg maintains that popular music differs from art music through its mass distribution strategy as well as its non-written distribution modes which produces distinct production and consumption patterns between these musical categories.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-15)

### Automatic recognition of genres

Main articles: [Automatic content recognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_content_recognition "Automatic content recognition") and [Music information retrieval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_information_retrieval "Music information retrieval")

Automatic methods of [musical similarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_similarity "Musical similarity") detection, based on [data mining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_mining "Data mining") and [co-occurrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-occurrence "Co-occurrence") analysis, have been developed to classify music titles for electronic music distribution.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-16)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-17)

Glenn McDonald, the employee of [The Echo Nest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Echo_Nest "The Echo Nest"), music intelligence and data platform, owned by [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), has created a categorical perception spectrum of genres and subgenres based on "an algorithmically generated, readability-adjusted scatter-plot of the musical genre-space, based on data tracked and analyzed for 5,315 genre-shaped distinctions by Spotify" called _[Every Noise at Once](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Every_Noise_at_Once "Every Noise at Once")._[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-guardian-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-19)

### Alternative approaches

Alternatively, music can be assessed on the three dimensions of "arousal", "valence", and "depth".[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-ECON-20) Arousal reflects physiological processes such as stimulation and relaxation (intense, forceful, abrasive, thrilling vs. gentle, calming, mellow), valence reflects emotion and mood processes (fun, happy, lively, enthusiastic, joyful vs. depressing, sad), and depth reflects cognitive processes (intelligent, sophisticated, inspiring, complex, poetic, deep, emotional, thoughtful vs. party music, danceable).[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-ECON-20) These help explain why many people like similar songs from different traditionally segregated genres.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-ECON-20)

Starting from the end of the 20th century, [Vincenzo Caporaletti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincenzo_Caporaletti "Vincenzo Caporaletti") has proposed a more comprehensive distinction of music genres based on the "formative medium" with which a music is created, that is the creative interface (cognitive milieu) employed by the artist. Following this framework, formative media may belong to two different matrixes: visual or audiotactile with regards to the role played in the creative process by the visual rationality or the bodily sensitivity and embodied cognition. The theory developed by Caporaletti, named Audiotactile Music Theory, categorises music in three different branches: 1) written music, like the so-called classical music, that is created using the visual matrix; 2) oral music (like [folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") or ethnic music before the advent of sound recording technologies); 3) Audiotactile music, which are process of production and transmission is pivoted around sound recording technologies (for example [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz"), pop, rock, [rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap "Rap") and so on). These last two branches are created by means of the above-mentioned audiotactile matrix in which the formative medium is the Audiotactile Principle.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-22)

## Major music genres

### Art music (Classical Music)

Main article: [Art music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_music "Art music")

See also: [List of art music traditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_art_music_traditions "List of art music traditions")

Art music primarily includes classical traditions, including both [contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_classical_music "Contemporary classical music") and historical classical music forms. Art music exists in many parts of the world. It emphasizes formal styles that invite technical and detailed deconstruction[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-23) and criticism, and demand focused attention from the listener. In Western practice, art music is considered primarily a written musical tradition,[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Arnold,_Denis-24) preserved in some form of [music notation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_notation "Musical notation") rather than being transmitted orally, by rote, or in recordings, as [popular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music") and [traditional music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_music "Traditional music") usually are.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Arnold,_Denis-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-25) Historically, most western art music has been written down using the standard forms of music notation that evolved in Europe, beginning well before the Renaissance and reaching its maturity in the Romantic period.

The identity of a "work" or "piece" of art music is usually defined by the notated version rather than by a particular performance and is primarily associated with the composer rather than the performer (though composers may leave performers with some opportunity for interpretation or improvisation). This is so particularly in the case of western classical music. Art music may include certain forms of [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz"), though some feel that jazz is primarily a form of popular music. The 1960s saw a wave of avant-garde experimentation in free jazz, represented by artists such as [Ornette Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornette_Coleman "Ornette Coleman"), [Sun Ra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Ra "Sun Ra"), [Albert Ayler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Ayler "Albert Ayler"), [Archie Shepp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Shepp "Archie Shepp") and [Don Cherry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cherry_(trumpeter) "Don Cherry (trumpeter)").[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-26) Additionally, avant-garde rock artists such as [Frank Zappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Zappa "Frank Zappa"), [Captain Beefheart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_Beefheart "Captain Beefheart"), and [the Residents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Residents "The Residents") released art music albums.

### Popular music

Main article: [Popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music")

Popular music is any musical style accessible to the general public and disseminated by the mass media. Musicologist and popular music specialist Philip Tagg defined the notion in the light of sociocultural and economical aspects:

> Popular music, unlike art music, is (1) conceived for mass distribution to large and often socioculturally heterogeneous groups of listeners, (2) stored and distributed in non-written form, (3) only possible in an industrial monetary economy where it becomes a commodity and (4) in capitalist societies, subject to the laws of 'free' enterprise\_ it should ideally sell as much as possible.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Analysing_Popular_Music_1982,_p._41-14)

The distinction between classical and popular music has sometimes been blurred in marginal areas[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-27) such as [minimalist music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimalist_music "Minimalist music") and light classics. Background music for films/movies often draws on both traditions. In this respect, music is like fiction, which likewise draws a distinction between [literary fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literary_fiction "Literary fiction") and [popular fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_fiction "Popular fiction") that is not always precise.

#### Country music

Main article: [Country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music")

Country music, also known as country and western (or simply country) and hillbilly music, is a genre of popular music that originated in the southern United States in the early 1920s. The origin of country music stems from European [folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") as well as ballads and dance tunes brought by British immigrants who combined these elements with [blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues "Blues") and [spirituals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirituals "Spirituals") of [African Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans") to create a separate musical form.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-28)

#### Electronic music

Main articles: [Electronic music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") and [electronic dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music")

Electronic music is music that employs [electronic musical instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_musical_instrument "Electronic musical instrument"), digital instruments, or [circuitry-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronics "Electronics") [music technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_technology "Music technology") in its creation. Contemporary electronic music includes many varieties and ranges from experimental art music to popular forms such as electronic dance music (EDM).

#### Funk

Main article: [Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk")

Funk is a music genre that originated in [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans") communities in the mid-1960s when musicians created a [rhythmic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm "Rhythm"), danceable new form of music through a mixture of soul, jazz, and rhythm and blues (R&B).

#### Hip-hop

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/DJ_Hypnotize_and_Baby_Cee.jpg/500px-DJ_Hypnotize_and_Baby_Cee.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DJ_Hypnotize_and_Baby_Cee.jpg) Two DJs practicing [turntablism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turntablism "Turntablism")

Main article: [Hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop")

Hip-hop or hip hop (originally known as disco rap, also as hip-hop music and sometimes rap music or rap) is a genre of music that emerged in the early 1970s alongside a hip-hop subculture built by the African-American and Latino communities of New York City. The musical style is characterized by the synthesis of a wide range of techniques, but rapping is frequent enough that it has nearly become a defining characteristic. Other key markers of the genre are the disc jockey (DJ), turntablism, scratching, beatboxing, and instrumental tracks. Cultural interchange has always been central to the hip-hop genre; it simultaneously borrows from its social environment while commenting on it. It can be broadly defined as a stylized rhythmic music that commonly accompanies [rapping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapping "Rapping"),[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-29) a rhythmic and rhyming speech that is chanted.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-30)

#### Jazz

Main article: [Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz")

Jazz is a music genre that originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans, Louisiana, United States, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with its roots in blues and ragtime.

#### Latin music

Main article: [Latin music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_music "Latin music")

Latin music is a genre of music that originated in the United States due to the growing influence of Latino Americans in the music industry. It is a term used by the music industry to describe music in a catch-all category for various music styles from [Ibero-America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibero-America "Ibero-America").

#### Pop music

Main article: [Pop music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music")

Pop is a genre of popular music that originated in its modern form during the mid-1950s in the United States and the United Kingdom. The terms popular music and pop music are often used interchangeably, although the former describes all music that is popular and includes many disparate styles.

#### Punk

Main article: [Punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock")

The aggressiveness of the musical and performative style, based on structural simplicity and the vigorous rhythms of rock'n'roll style, reinforced the challenging and provocative character, within the universe of modern music.

#### Reggae

Main article: [Reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae")

Reggae music, originating from the late 1960s [Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica "Jamaica"), is a genre of music that was originally used by Jamaicans to define themselves with their lifestyle and social aspects.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-31) The meaning behind reggae songs tend to be about love, faith or a higher power, and freedom.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-32) Reggae music is important to [Jamaican culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Jamaica "Culture of Jamaica") as it has been used as inspiration for many third world liberation movements. [Bob Marley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Marley "Bob Marley"), an artist primarily known for reggae music, was honored by Zimbabwe's 1980 Independence celebration due to his music giving inspirations to freedom fighters.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] The music genre of reggae is known to incorporate stylistic techniques from [rhythm and blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues"), [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz"), African, Caribbean, and other genres as well but what makes reggae unique are the vocals and lyrics.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] The vocals tend to be sung in [Jamaican Patois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaican_Patois "Jamaican Patois"), [Jamaican English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaican_English "Jamaican English"), and [Iyaric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iyaric "Iyaric") dialects. The lyrics of reggae music usually tend to raise political awareness and on cultural perspectives.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-33)

#### Rock music

Main article: [Rock music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music")

Rock music is a broad genre of popular music that originated as " [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll")" in the United States in the late 1940s and early 1950s, developing into a range of different styles in the mid-1960s and later, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom.

#### Heavy Metal/Metal music

Main article: [Heavy metal music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music")

Heavy metal evolved from [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock"), [psychedelic rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychedelic_rock "Psychedelic rock"), and [blues rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues_rock "Blues rock") in late 1960s and 1970s with notable acts such as [Black Sabbath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sabbath "Black Sabbath"), [Judas Priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judas_Priest "Judas Priest") and [Motörhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mot%C3%B6rhead "Motörhead"). The popularity of heavy metal soared in the 1980s with bands such as [Iron Maiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Maiden "Iron Maiden"), [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica") and [Guns N' Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_N'_Roses "Guns N' Roses"). It has a rougher style and heavier sound than other forms of rock music, with notable subgenres such as [thrash metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrash_metal "Thrash metal"), [hair metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_metal "Hair metal") and [death metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_metal "Death metal").\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

#### Soca

Main article: [Soca music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soca_music "Soca music")

**Soca music**, or the "soul of calypso", is a genre of music that originated in [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago "Trinidad and Tobago") in the 1970s. It is considered an offshoot of [calypso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calypso_music "Calypso music"), with influences from [Afro-Trinidadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro%E2%80%93Trinidadians_and_Tobagonians "Afro–Trinidadians and Tobagonians") and [Indo-Trinidadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo%E2%80%93Trinidadians_and_Tobagonians "Indo–Trinidadians and Tobagonians") rhythms.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-34) It was created by [Ras Shorty I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Shorty_I "Ras Shorty I") (or Lord Shorty)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-35)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-36) in an effort to revive traditional calypso, the popularity of which had been declining amongst younger generations in Trinidad due to the rise in popularity of [reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae") from Jamaica and [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk") from the United States. From the 1980s onward, soca has developed into a range of new styles.

#### Soul music and R&B

Main articles: [Soul music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and [rhythm and blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues")

Soul music became a musical genre that came to include a wide variety of R&B-based music styles from the pop R&B acts at [Motown Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motown_Records "Motown Records") in Detroit, such as [the Temptations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Temptations "The Temptations"), [Gladys Knight & the Pips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gladys_Knight_&_the_Pips "Gladys Knight & the Pips"), [Marvin Gaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Gaye "Marvin Gaye") and [Four Tops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Tops "Four Tops"), to " [deep soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_soul "Deep soul")" singers such as [Percy Sledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percy_Sledge "Percy Sledge") and [James Carr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Carr_(musician) "James Carr (musician)").[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-Motown_Museum-37)

#### Polka

Main article: [Polka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polka "Polka")

The polka is originally a Czech dance and genre of dance music familiar throughout Europe and the Americas.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-38)

### Religious music

Main article: [Religious music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_music "Religious music")

Religious music (also referred as sacred music) is music performed or composed for religious use or through religious influence. [Gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_music "Gospel music"), spiritual, and [Christian music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_music "Christian music") are examples of religious music.

### Traditional and folk music

Main articles: [Folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") and [contemporary folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_folk_music "Contemporary folk music")

[![A picture of a red and black button accordion](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8c/Sonolite.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sonolite.jpg) [Piano accordion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_accordion "Piano accordion"): Italian instrument used in several cultures

Traditional and folk music are very similar categories, but it is widely accepted that traditional music encompasses folk music.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-39) According to the [ICTM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Council_for_Traditional_Music "International Council for Traditional Music") (International Council for Traditional Music), traditional music are songs and tunes that have been performed over a long period of time (usually several generations) **.**[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-40)

The [folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") genre is classified as the music that is orally passed from one generation to another. Usually, the artist is unknown, and there are several versions of the same song.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-41) The genre is transmitted by singing, listening and dancing to popular songs. This type of communication allows culture to transmit the styles (pitches and cadences) as well as the context it was developed.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-:0-42)

Culturally transmitting folk songs maintain rich evidence about the period of history when they were created and the social class in which they developed.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-43) Some examples of the Folk Genre can be seen in the [folk music of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_folk_music "English folk music") and [Turkish folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_folk_music "Turkish folk music"). English folk music has developed since the [medieval period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages") and has been transmitted from that time until today. Similarly, Turkish folk music relates to all the civilizations that once passed thorough Turkey, thereby being a world reference since the east–west tensions during the [Early Modern Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Modern_history "Early Modern history").\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

Traditional folk music usually refers to songs composed in the twentieth century, which tend to be written as universal truths and big issues of the time they were composed.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-44) Artists including [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan"); [Peter, Paul and Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter,_Paul_and_Mary "Peter, Paul and Mary"); [James Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Taylor "James Taylor"); and [Leonard Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Cohen "Leonard Cohen"), transformed folk music to what it is known today.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-45) Newer composers such as [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") (pop folk) and [the Lumineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lumineers "The Lumineers") (American folk) are examples of contemporary folk music, which has been recorded and adapted to the new way of listening to music (online)—unlike the traditional way of orally transmitting music.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-46)

Each country in the world, in some cases each region, district and community, has its own folk music style. The sub-divisions of folk genre are developed by each place, cultural identity and history.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-47) Because the music is developed in different places, many of the instruments are characteristic to location and population—but some are used everywhere: [button](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Button_accordion "Button accordion") or [piano accordion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_accordion "Piano accordion"), different types of flutes or trumpets, [banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banjo "Banjo"), and [ukulele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukulele "Ukulele"). Both French and Scottish folk music use related instruments such as the [fiddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddle "Fiddle"), the harp and variations of [bagpipes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagpipes "Bagpipes").[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-48)

### Social influences on music selection

Since music has become more easily accessible ( [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes"), YouTube, etc.), more people have begun listening to a broader and wider range of music styles.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-:02-49) In addition, social identity also plays a large role in music preference. Personality is a key contributor for music selection. Those who consider themselves to be "rebels" will tend to choose heavier music styles like [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") or [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock"), while those who consider themselves to be more "relaxed" or "laid back" will tend to choose lighter music styles like [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") or classical music.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-:02-49) According to one model, there are five main factors that exist that underlie music preferences that are genre-free,\[ _[contradictory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:All_self-contradictory_articles "Category:All self-contradictory articles")_\] and reflect emotional/affective responses.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-:1-50) These five factors are:

1. A Mellow factor consisting of smooth and relaxing styles (jazz, classical, etc.).
2. An Urban factor defined largely by rhythmic and percussive music (rap, [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music"), [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk"), etc.).
3. A Sophisticated factor ( [operatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opera_music "Opera music"), [world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_music "World music"), etc.)
4. An Intensity factor that is defined by forceful, loud, and energetic music (rock, metal, etc.).
5. A campestral factor, which refers to singer-songwriter genres and country.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-:1-50)

### Individual and situational influences

Studies have shown that while women prefer more treble oriented music, men prefer to listen to bass-heavy music. A preference for bass-heavy music is sometimes paired with [borderline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borderline_personality_disorder "Borderline personality disorder") and [antisocial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisocial_personality_disorder "Antisocial personality disorder") personalities.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-51)

Age is another strong factor that contributes to musical preference. Evidence is available that shows that music preference can change as one gets older.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-52) A Canadian study showed that adolescents show greater interest in pop music artists while adults and the elderly population prefer classic genres such as rock, opera, and [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz").[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre#cite_note-53)

(divorced)​ | | | | Website | [mccoytyner.com](http://mccoytyner.com/) | | | | Relatives | [Jarvis Tyner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarvis_Tyner "Jarvis Tyner") (brother) | | | Musical artist **Alfred McCoy Tyner** (December 11, 1938–March 6, 2020) was an American [jazz pianist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_piano "Jazz piano") and composer known for his work with the [John Coltrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Coltrane "John Coltrane") Quartet from 1960 to 1965 and his long solo career afterward.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-1) He was an [NEA Jazz Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEA_Jazz_Masters "NEA Jazz Masters") and a five-time [Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy "Grammy") Award winner. Tyner has been widely imitated and is one of the most recognizable and influential jazz pianists of all time.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-nytdeath-2) ## Early life and education \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=McCoy_Tyner&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")\] Tyner was born on December 11, 1938,[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-McCoy_Tyner:_The_Pianist-4) in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), Pennsylvania, United States, the eldest of Jarvis and Beatrice (née Stevenson) Tyner's three children.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Chinen-5) Tyner was encouraged to study piano by his mother, who had installed a piano at her beauty salon. At the age of 13, he began piano lessons at the [Granoff School of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granoff_School_of_Music "Granoff School of Music"), where he also studied [music theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_theory "Music theory") and [harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony "Harmony"). By the time he was 15 years old, music had become the center of his life.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-NEA-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-7) Tyner's decision to study piano was reinforced when he encountered [bebop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bebop "Bebop") pianist [Bud Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Powell "Bud Powell"), a neighbor of the Tyner family.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Collar-8) Another major influence on Tyner's playing was [Thelonious Monk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thelonious_Monk "Thelonious Monk"), whose percussive attacks informed Tyner's style.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-McCoy_Tyner:_The_Pianist-4) During his teens, Tyner led his own group, the Houserockers.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Heckman-9) When he was 17, Tyner converted to [Ahmadiyya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmadiyya "Ahmadiyya") and changed his name to Suleiman Saud,[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-11) although he continued to perform as "McCoy Tyner".[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Collar-8) ## Early career and the John Coltrane Quartet \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=McCoy_Tyner&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Early career and the John Coltrane Quartet")\] [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/McCoy_Keystone.jpg/250px-McCoy_Keystone.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:McCoy_Keystone.jpg) Tyner at [Keystone Korner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystone_Korner "Keystone Korner") in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), in March 1981[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/McCoyTynerandRaviColtrane.jpg/250px-McCoyTynerandRaviColtrane.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:McCoyTynerandRaviColtrane.jpg) Tyner with [Ravi Coltrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravi_Coltrane "Ravi Coltrane") at the [Newport Jazz Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Jazz_Festival "Newport Jazz Festival") in [Newport, Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport,_Rhode_Island "Newport, Rhode Island"), in August 2005[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/McCoy_Tyner_04.jpg/250px-McCoy_Tyner_04.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:McCoy_Tyner_04.jpg) Tyner with his quartet at Jazz Alley in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"), in April 2012 Tyner began playing professionally in Philadelphia with local artists such as [Lee Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Morgan "Lee Morgan") and [Jimmy Heath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Heath "Jimmy Heath"), participating in the city's modern jazz scene.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Chinen-5)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Collar-8) He first met [John Coltrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Coltrane "John Coltrane"), who eventually became "like a big brother" to Tyner,[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Milkowski-12) in the summer of 1955. They kept in touch, played together occasionally, and had an understanding that if Coltrane ever formed a group of his own, Tyner would be the pianist.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-13) In 1960, Tyner joined [The Jazztet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Jazztet "The Jazztet") led by [Benny Golson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Golson "Benny Golson") and [Art Farmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Farmer "Art Farmer") and recorded on the group's debut album, _[Meet the Jazztet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_the_Jazztet "Meet the Jazztet")_. Around the same time, Coltrane left [Miles Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_Davis "Miles Davis")'s group and formed a quartet of his own, but because he was friends with Golson, he was reluctant to ask Tyner to leave The Jazztet. Encouraged by his wife, Naima, Coltrane eventually asked Tyner what he wanted to do.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-14) After six months with The Jazztet, Tyner joined the John Coltrane Quartet, which then included bassist [Steve Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Davis_(bassist) "Steve Davis (bassist)") and drummer [Elvin Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvin_Jones "Elvin Jones"). Tyner worked with the band during its extended run at the Jazz Gallery, replacing [Steve Kuhn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Kuhn "Steve Kuhn").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Collar-8)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-15) Reflecting on the situation later, Tyner said: "There were probably some bad feelings at first with the Jazztet, but I think they understood better later on. John's group was where I belonged."[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-16) Coltrane had already recorded Tyner's composition "The Believer" on January 10, 1958, which became the title track of [Prestige Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prestige_Records "Prestige Records")' 1964 [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Believer_(John_Coltrane_album) "The Believer (John Coltrane album)") under Coltrane's name.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-18) The band toured almost nonstop between 1961 and 1965 and went through personnel changes on bass, with [Reggie Workman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Workman "Reggie Workman") replacing Davis and then [Jimmy Garrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Garrison "Jimmy Garrison") replacing Workman, establishing the quartet's classic lineup. The group recorded many albums widely considered jazz classics, including _[My Favorite Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Favorite_Things_(John_Coltrane_album) "My Favorite Things (John Coltrane album)")_ (1961) for [Atlantic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Records "Atlantic Records") and _[Coltrane "Live" at the Village Vanguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coltrane_%22Live%22_at_the_Village_Vanguard "Coltrane \"Live\" at the Village Vanguard")_ (1962), _[Ballads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballads_(John_Coltrane_album) "Ballads (John Coltrane album)")_ (1963), _[John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Coltrane_and_Johnny_Hartman "John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman")_ (1963), _[Live at Birdland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_Birdland_(John_Coltrane_album) "Live at Birdland (John Coltrane album)")_ (1964), _[Crescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crescent_(John_Coltrane_album) "Crescent (John Coltrane album)")_ (1964), _[A Love Supreme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Love_Supreme "A Love Supreme")_ (1964), and _[The John Coltrane Quartet Plays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_John_Coltrane_Quartet_Plays "The John Coltrane Quartet Plays")_ (1965) for [Impulse! Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impulse!_Records "Impulse! Records").[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-19) _A Love Supreme_, in particular, is recognized by consensus as one of the greatest jazz albums ever made.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-20) Tyner said, "the band had reached a very high level by that time .... \[Coltrane\] wanted to dig deep and bring us up to another level. And that's what he did."[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Milkowski-12) While in Coltrane's group, Tyner also recorded albums as a leader, including trio recordings, such as his debut album, _[Inception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inception_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Inception (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1962). In late 1962 and the first half of 1963, producer [Bob Thiele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Thiele "Bob Thiele") asked Tyner to record other more straightforward jazz albums as a leader. These include _[Reaching Fourth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reaching_Fourth "Reaching Fourth")_ (1963), _[Nights of Ballads & Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nights_of_Ballads_&_Blues "Nights of Ballads & Blues")_ (1963), _[Today and Tomorrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_and_Tomorrow_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Today and Tomorrow (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1964), and _[McCoy Tyner Plays Ellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner_Plays_Ellington "McCoy Tyner Plays Ellington")_ (1965).[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-21) Tyner also appeared as a sideman on many [Blue Note Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Note_Records "Blue Note Records") albums of the 1960s, including classic recordings with [Freddie Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Hubbard "Freddie Hubbard"), [Wayne Shorter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Shorter "Wayne Shorter"), and [Joe Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Henderson "Joe Henderson"), although he was often credited as "etc." on these albums' covers to respect his contract with Impulse!.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Collar-8) Tyner's maximalist playing style developed in close contact with Coltrane.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Collar-8)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Linna-22) In 2019, Sami Linna of the [University of the Arts Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Arts_Helsinki "University of the Arts Helsinki") wrote that Coltrane described the two different directions in his playing as "playing chordally (vertically) or melodically (horizontally)". Linna suggests that "Tyner would eventually find a way of dealing with the two directions simultaneously, in a manner that was supportive and complementary yet original and slightly different from Coltrane's approach." After 1960, Coltrane did not hire anyone to replace Tyner if he was unavailable; between the time Tyner joined the group (around the end of May 1960) and left (December 1965), no other pianist accompanied Coltrane.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Linna-22) Tyner's involvement with Coltrane ended in 1965. Coltrane's music was becoming much more atonal and free; he had also augmented his quartet with additional percussion players who threatened to drown out both Tyner and Jones, who left the following year. Tyner commented, "I didn't see myself making any contribution to that music. ... All I could hear was a lot of noise. I didn't have any feeling for the music, and when I don't have feelings, I don't play."[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-23) [Alice Coltrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Coltrane "Alice Coltrane") then replaced Tyner as the group's pianist.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-24) ## Later solo career \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=McCoy_Tyner&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Later solo career")\] In 1966, Tyner rehearsed with a new trio and embarked on a career as a bandleader.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-25) Inconsistent work initially discouraged him and led him to consider taking a day job to support his family, and he inquired about becoming a taxi driver.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-26) Eventually, Tyner established himself as a viable solo artist through a series of [post-bop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-bop "Post-bop") albums as a leader Blue Note released between 1967 and 1970. These include _[The Real McCoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Real_McCoy_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "The Real McCoy (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1967), _[Tender Moments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tender_Moments "Tender Moments")_ (1967), _[Time for Tyner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_for_Tyner "Time for Tyner")_ (1968) with vibraphonist [Bobby Hutcherson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Hutcherson "Bobby Hutcherson"), _[Expansions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expansions_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Expansions (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1968), and _[Extensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extensions_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Extensions (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1970). Tyner then signed with [Milestone Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milestone_Records "Milestone Records"), where he developed an excellent working relationship with jazz producer [Orrin Keepnews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orrin_Keepnews "Orrin Keepnews"), who had previously worked closely with [Thelonious Monk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thelonious_Monk "Thelonious Monk") and [Bill Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Evans "Bill Evans").[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Smithsonian-27) Tyner's first album with his new label, _[Sahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Sahara (McCoy Tyner album)")_, earned him his first two [Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy "Grammy") nominations and was named Album of the Year in the _[DownBeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DownBeat "DownBeat")_ critics' poll.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Concord-28) Tyner recorded 19 albums for the label before moving to [Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"), including a solo piano tribute to Coltrane titled _[Echoes of a Friend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echoes_of_a_Friend "Echoes of a Friend")_ (1972), a number of small-group records like _[Enlightenment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enlightenment_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Enlightenment (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1973) and _[Sama Layuca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sama_Layuca "Sama Layuca")_ (1974), and two orchestral albums, _[Song of the New World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_New_World "Song of the New World")_ (1973) and _[Fly with the Wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fly_with_the_Wind "Fly with the Wind")_ (1976), both featuring flutist [Hubert Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_Laws "Hubert Laws"), various other wind instruments, and full string sections.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-29) Tyner did the orchestrations, drawing on [Walter Piston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Piston "Walter Piston")'s book _Harmony_.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-30) Front-line players featured on Tyner's Milestone recordings include [Gary Bartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Bartz "Gary Bartz"), [Sonny Fortune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonny_Fortune "Sonny Fortune"), [Azar Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azar_Lawrence "Azar Lawrence"), and [Woody Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Shaw "Woody Shaw").[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Concord-28) Tyner's recordings for Blue Note and Milestone often took Coltrane Quartet's music as a point of departure; as Tyner said, "a lot of what I learned from \[Coltrane\] transferred" to his later work.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Milkowski-12) Tyner also incorporated African and East Asian elements into his music. On _Sahara_, he played [_koto_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koto_(musical_instrument) "Koto (musical instrument)") in addition to piano, flute, and percussion. On the trio recording _[Trident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trident_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Trident (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1975), with bassist [Ron Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Carter "Ron Carter") and Elvin Jones, Tyner played the [harpsichord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harpsichord "Harpsichord") and [celesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celesta "Celesta"), instruments rarely heard in jazz.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-31) These albums have been cited as examples of innovative 1970s jazz that was neither [fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_fusion "Jazz fusion") nor [free jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_jazz "Free jazz"). Unlike many jazz keyboardists of his generation, Tyner rarely used [electronic keyboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_keyboard "Electronic keyboard") or [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer"), saying, "To me, electronic instruments have more of an artificial sound. Emotionally I couldn't function on them."[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-32) In 1982, Tyner and a number of other notable jazz pianists participated in the recording _Bill Evans: A Tribute_ (Avion Records). He played an 8½-minute solo version of Evans's "We Will Meet Again" in honor of his deceased colleague.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-33) During the 1980s and 1990s, Tyner performed and recorded in a trio including [Avery Sharpe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avery_Sharpe "Avery Sharpe") on bass[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-34) and [Louis Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Hayes "Louis Hayes"),[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-35) then [Aaron Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Scott_(musician) "Aaron Scott (musician)"), on drums.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-36) He also recorded a trilogy of solo or solo-with-guests albums for Blue Note, beginning with _[Revelations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revelations_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Revelations (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1988)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-37) and culminating in _[Soliloquy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soliloquy_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Soliloquy (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1991).[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-38) In addition, he recorded another album with Bobby Hutcherson, _[Manhattan Moods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Moods "Manhattan Moods")_, in 1993. After signing with [Telarc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telarc_International_Corporation "Telarc International Corporation"), he recorded, between 1998 and 2003, an album of [Latin music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner_and_the_Latin_All-Stars "McCoy Tyner and the Latin All-Stars"), a [trio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner_with_Stanley_Clarke_and_Al_Foster "McCoy Tyner with Stanley Clarke and Al Foster") with [Stanley Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Clarke "Stanley Clarke") and [Al Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Foster "Al Foster"), a [solo album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_Roots "Jazz Roots") honoring fellow jazz piano legends from [Earl Hines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Hines "Earl Hines") to [Keith Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Jarrett "Keith Jarrett"), a [new album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_of_Giants "Land of Giants") with Hutcherson, and, finally, a quintet album, _[Illuminations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminations_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Illuminations (McCoy Tyner album)")_, with [Terence Blanchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terence_Blanchard "Terence Blanchard") and [Gary Bartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Bartz "Gary Bartz"). Tyner's last three albums were recorded for McCoy Tyner Music under the auspices of [Half Note Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_Note_Records "Half Note Records").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Milkowski-12) These include a [quartet recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartet_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Quartet (McCoy Tyner album)") with [Joe Lovano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lovano "Joe Lovano"), an [album featuring various guest guitarists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitars_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Guitars (McCoy Tyner album)") from [Bill Frisell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Frisell "Bill Frisell") to [Derek Trucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Trucks "Derek Trucks"), and a [live solo album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solo:_Live_from_San_Francisco "Solo: Live from San Francisco"). Tyner stopped making recordings in 2007 even though he lived another 13 years. He continued to play gigs for a while after that but then quietly retired.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Whitehead-39) Tyner composed widely. His most frequently covered piece is "You Taught My Heart to Sing" (1985), for which [Sammy Cahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Cahn "Sammy Cahn") wrote lyrics. Other compositions of his that have been recorded by a number of artists include "Aisha" (1961), "Inception" and "Effendi" (1962), and "Passion Dance", "Contemplation", "Search for Peace", and "Blues on the Corner", all from the 1967 album _[The Real McCoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Real_McCoy_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "The Real McCoy (McCoy Tyner album)")_.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-40) ## Personal life \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=McCoy_Tyner&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Personal life")\] Tyner married Aisha Saud while they were both in their teens; they had three sons. The marriage ended in divorce.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-WPobit-41)[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-42)[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-43) Tyner's younger brother [Jarvis Tyner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarvis_Tyner "Jarvis Tyner") was executive vice-chairman of the [Communist Party USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_USA "Communist Party USA").[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Ratliff-44) ## Death \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=McCoy_Tyner&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Death")\] Tyner died at his home in [Bergenfield, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergenfield,_New_Jersey "Bergenfield, New Jersey"), on March 6, 2020. He was 81.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-WPobit-41)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-nytdeath-2) No cause of death was given, but he had been in ill health.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-45) ## Influence and playing style \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=McCoy_Tyner&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Influence and playing style")\] Tyner is considered one of the most influential jazz pianists of the late 20th century, an honor he earned during and after his time with Coltrane.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-46) Tyner, who was left-handed, played with a low bass left hand and raised his arm high above the keyboard for emphatic attacks. His right-hand soloing was detached and [staccato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staccato "Staccato"). His melodic vocabulary was rich, ranging from raw [blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues "Blues") to complex [superimposed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_structure "Upper structure") [pentatonic scales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentatonic_scale "Pentatonic scale"); his approach to chord voicing (most characteristically by fourths) influenced contemporary jazz pianists such as [Herbie Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Hancock "Herbie Hancock"), [Chick Corea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea "Chick Corea"), [John Hicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hicks_(pianist) "John Hicks (pianist)"), and [Kenny Barron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Barron "Kenny Barron").[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-47) Some of Tyner's harmonic techniques have been connected to [Claude Debussy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Debussy "Claude Debussy"),[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-48) one of Tyner's favorite composers.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-49) Tyner's extensive use of [non-tertiary harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartal_and_quintal_harmony "Quartal and quintal harmony") has also led to comparisons with the work of [Paul Hindemith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Hindemith "Paul Hindemith"), but Tyner disavowed any direct influence in that case.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Smithsonian-27) Tyner did say he found inspiration in the music of [Igor Stravinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Stravinsky "Igor Stravinsky"), [Duke Ellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Ellington "Duke Ellington"), and [Art Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Tatum "Art Tatum") as well as in music from Japan, Turkey, and Africa.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-50) In 1983, Tyner's colleague [Randy Weston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Weston "Randy Weston") said of him: "He's showing the way to the future, yet he's maintaining the tradition, the rhythmic quality, the spiritual vitality, the humor, the sadness. ... McCoy is on the right track."[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-51) [Vijay Iyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijay_Iyer "Vijay Iyer"), a younger jazz pianist who acknowledges Tyner's influence, said, "I've studied Tyner's fluidity, hard groove, and deep sonorities for decades. In the wake of his passing in 2020, I was again revisiting the moments in his playing that were formative for me."[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-52) Jazz historian [Kevin Whitehead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Whitehead "Kevin Whitehead") wrote that Tyner "plays thundering, ambiguous chords under fast, right-hand melodies often based on five-note scales, a marker in jazz of African roots. His sound was heavy, but buoyant, billowing like blue smoke. His piano could toll like church bells. And he could really move, too."[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Whitehead-39) In his _History of Jazz_, [Ted Gioia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Gioia "Ted Gioia") sums up Tyner's style as follows:[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-53) > Blessed with a crisp, clean piano attack and a sure sense of melodic development, Tyner could have been a premier hard-bop pianist. But alongside Coltrane, Tyner gradually grew to be much more. Where other pianists would have backed Coltrane's horn lines with throwaway comping chords, Tyner challenged the soloist with a tsunami of sound. ... Tyner delighted in ambiguous voicings, liberally spiced with suspended fourths that rarely resolved, often played with a thunderous two-handed attack that seemed destined to leave permanent marks in the keys. ... Single-note lines, leavened with wide, often unpredictable interval leaps, jostled with sweeping [arpeggios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arpeggios "Arpeggios"), cascading runs, reverberating [tremolos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tremolos "Tremolos"). His touch at the piano, which originally possessed brittle sharpness, took on volume and depth, eventually emerging as one of the fullest and most easily identifiable keyboard sounds in jazz. Tyner's career continued to flourish long after leaving Coltrane, and ... would influence many jazz pianists who came of age during that period. But though others mimicked Tyner's mannerisms, his voicings, and modal runs, these acolytes seldom approached the intensity of the original. [Grateful Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grateful_Dead "Grateful Dead") rhythm guitarist [Bob Weir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Weir "Bob Weir") has also cited Tyner as an influence on his playing.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-Relix-54) ## Awards and honors \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=McCoy_Tyner&action=edit§ion=7 "Edit section: Awards and honors")\] Tyner was named a 2002 [NEA Jazz Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEA_Jazz_Master "NEA Jazz Master") by the [National Endowment for the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Arts "National Endowment for the Arts").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-NEA-6) He won five [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), all relatively late in his career: _[The Turning Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Turning_Point_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "The Turning Point (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1992) and _[Journey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journey_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Journey (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1993) both won for [Best Large Jazz Ensemble Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Large_Jazz_Ensemble_Album "Grammy Award for Best Large Jazz Ensemble Album"), and _[Blues for Coltrane: A Tribute to John Coltrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues_for_Coltrane:_A_Tribute_to_John_Coltrane "Blues for Coltrane: A Tribute to John Coltrane")_ (1987), _[Infinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinity_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Infinity (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (1995), and _[Illuminations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminations_(McCoy_Tyner_album) "Illuminations (McCoy Tyner album)")_ (2004) all won in the category of [Best Instrumental Jazz Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Jazz_Instrumental_Album "Grammy Award for Best Jazz Instrumental Album").[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-55) Tyner was awarded an [Honorary Doctorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_degree "Honorary 10th,[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-57) and 11th annual Independent Music Awards.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner#cite_note-58) [Steinway & Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steinway_&_Sons "Steinway & Sons") conferred a special gold medallion to Tyner for his 50 years as a Steinway # Steppenwolf (band) Steppenwolf (band) Canadian–American rock group | Steppenwolf | | --- | | [![Steppenwolf in 1971 (L–R: Goldy McJohn, Jerry Edmonton, John Kay, Larry Byrom, George Biondo)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/aa/Steppenwolf_%281971%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Steppenwolf_(1971).png "Steppenwolf in 1971 (L–R: Goldy McJohn, Jerry Edmonton, John Kay, Larry Byrom, George Biondo)")
