- [Five Peace Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_Peace_Band "Five Peace Band") | | | | Website | [chickcorea.com](http://chickcorea.com/) | Musical artist **Armando Anthony** " **Chick**" **Corea** (June 12, 1941 – February 9, 2021) was an American [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") pianist, composer, bandleader, and occasional percussionist.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Siemaszko-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-ALLMUSIC-3) His compositions " [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_(instrumental) "Spain (instrumental)")", " [500 Miles High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/500_Miles_High "500 Miles High")", "La Fiesta", "Armando's Rhumba", and " [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_(composition) "Windows (composition)")" are considered [jazz standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_standard "Jazz standard").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-4) As a member of the [Miles Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_Davis "Miles Davis") band in the late 1960s, Corea participated in the birth of [jazz fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_fusion "Jazz fusion"). In the 1970s he formed [Return to Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_to_Forever "Return to Forever").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-ALLMUSIC-3) Along with [McCoy Tyner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCoy_Tyner "McCoy Tyner"), [Herbie Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Hancock "Herbie Hancock") and [Keith Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Jarrett "Keith Jarrett"), Corea is considered one of the foremost pianists of the post- [John Coltrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Coltrane "John Coltrane") era.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-losangelestimes-5) Corea continued to collaborate frequently while exploring different musical styles throughout the 1980s and 1990s. He won 29 [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") and has been nominated for the award 79 times.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Grammy-6) ## Early life and education \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chick_Corea&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")\] Armando Corea was born in [Chelsea, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea,_Massachusetts "Chelsea, Massachusetts"),[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-7)\[ _[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_\] to parents Anna (née Zaccone) and Armando J. Corea.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Siemaszko-2)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-NYTOBIT-8) His father's family was from [Albi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albi,_Calabria "Albi, Calabria"), a commune in the [Province of Catanzaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Catanzaro "Province of Catanzaro") in the [Calabria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabria "Calabria") region of Italy.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-10) His father, a trumpeter who led a [Dixieland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixieland "Dixieland") band in Boston in the 1930s and 1940s, introduced him to the piano at the age of four.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-11) Surrounded by jazz, he was influenced at an early age by [bebop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bebop "Bebop") and musicians such as [Dizzy Gillespie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dizzy_Gillespie "Dizzy Gillespie"), [Charlie Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Parker "Charlie Parker"), [Bud Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Powell "Bud Powell"), [Horace Silver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace_Silver "Horace Silver"), and [Lester Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lester_Young "Lester Young").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-12) He came into possession of a [drumset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drumset "Drumset") at age 11,[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Ted-13) and would occasionally play drums for the rest of his career.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-14) Corea developed his piano skills while exploring music on his own. At first, his father taught him piano, but eventually, the elder Corea thought it proper that his son receive instruction from a professional teacher. At the age of eight, he began taking formal lessons with Italian concert pianist Salvatore Sullo. Sullo was indifferent to the young Corea's passion for jazz, instead teaching him to play [classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music "Classical music") piano, but being introduced to classical music helped spark Corea's interest in musical composition.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Ted-13) Given a black tuxedo by his father, he started playing gigs while still in high school. He enjoyed listening to [Herb Pomeroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herb_Pomeroy "Herb Pomeroy")'s band at the time and had a trio that played Horace Silver's music at a local jazz club. He eventually moved to New York City, where he studied music at [Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University "Columbia University"), then transferred to the [Juilliard School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juilliard_School "Juilliard School"). He later dropped out so he could spend more time playing gigs.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-NYTOBIT-8) ## Career \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chick_Corea&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Career")\] Corea began his professional recording and touring career in the early 1960s with [Mongo Santamaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongo_Santamaria "Mongo Santamaria"), [Willie Bobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Bobo "Willie Bobo"), [Blue Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Mitchell "Blue Mitchell"), [Herbie Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Mann "Herbie Mann"), and [Stan Getz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Getz "Stan Getz"). In 1966, he recorded his debut album, _[Tones for Joan's Bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tones_for_Joan's_Bones "Tones for Joan's Bones")_. In March 1968, he recorded the highly regarded trio album, _[Now He Sings, Now He Sobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Now_He_Sings,_Now_He_Sobs "Now He Sings, Now He Sobs")_, with drummer [Roy Haynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Haynes "Roy Haynes") and bassist [Miroslav Vitouš](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miroslav_Vitou%C5%A1 "Miroslav Vitouš").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-ALLMUSIC-3) In the fall of 1968,[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Early-15) Corea began recording and touring with [Miles Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_Davis "Miles Davis"), appearing on the widely praised Davis studio albums _[Filles de Kilimanjaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filles_de_Kilimanjaro "Filles de Kilimanjaro")_, _[In a Silent Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_a_Silent_Way "In a Silent Way")_, _[Bitches Brew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitches_Brew "Bitches Brew")_, and _[On the Corner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_the_Corner "On the Corner")_. He also appeared on later compilation albums [_Big Fun_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Fun_(Miles_Davis_album) "Big Fun (Miles Davis album)"), [_Water Babies_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_Babies_(album) "Water Babies (album)"), and _[Circle in the Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_in_the_Round "Circle in the Round")_. He left Davis' band shortly after its performance at the [1970 Isle of Wight Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Isle_of_Wight_Festival "1970 Isle of Wight Festival").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Early-15) Bassist [Dave Holland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Holland_(bassist) "Dave Holland (bassist)") departed the Davis group with Corea to form their own group, [Circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_(jazz_band) "Circle (jazz band)"), with [multireedist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multireedist "Multireedist") [Anthony Braxton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Braxton "Anthony Braxton") and drummer [Barry Altschul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Altschul "Barry Altschul"). They were active from 1970 to 1971, and recorded on [Blue Note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Note_Records "Blue Note Records") and [ECM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECM_Records "ECM Records").[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-16) In 1971, Corea, at the behest of ECM producer [Manfred Eicher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manfred_Eicher "Manfred Eicher"), began playing solo piano, recording the sessions that became _[Piano Improvisations Vol. 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_Improvisations_Vol._1 "Piano Improvisations Vol. 1")_ and _[Piano Improvisations Vol. 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_Improvisations_Vol._2 "Piano Improvisations Vol. 2")_ in April of that year.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-17) In 1974, Corea collaborated with Richie Grasso on the latter's album _Season of Grace_, produced by [Morris Levy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Levy "Morris Levy")'s [Tiger Lily Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Lily_Records "Tiger Lily Records").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-18) ### Jazz fusion \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chick_Corea&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Jazz fusion")\] [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Chick_Corea_held_an_open_performance_at_the_Sultan%27s_Pool_in_Jerusalem%2C_attended_by_thousands_of_Israelis_%28FL62915891%29.jpg/330px-Chick_Corea_held_an_open_performance_at_the_Sultan%27s_Pool_in_Jerusalem%2C_attended_by_thousands_of_Israelis_%28FL62915891%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chick_Corea_held_an_open_performance_at_the_Sultan's_Pool_in_Jerusalem,_attended_by_thousands_of_Israelis_(FL62915891).jpg) Corea during a performance at [Sultan's Pool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan's_Pool "Sultan's Pool") in [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem"), 1981 Named after their eponymous 1972 album, Corea's [Return to Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_to_Forever "Return to Forever") band combined acoustic and electronic instrumentation, and initially drew upon Hispanic music styles more than rock music. On their first two records, the group consisted of [Flora Purim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flora_Purim "Flora Purim") on vocals and percussion, [Joe Farrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Farrell "Joe Farrell") on flute and soprano saxophone, Miles Davis bandmate [Airto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airto_Moreira "Airto Moreira") on drums and percussion, and [Stanley Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Clarke "Stanley Clarke") on acoustic double bass.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-ALLMUSIC-3) Drummer [Lenny White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenny_White "Lenny White") and guitarist [Bill Connors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Connors "Bill Connors") later joined Corea and Clarke to form the second version of the group, which blended the earlier Latin music elements with rock and funk-oriented music. This incarnation of the band recorded the album _[Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymn_of_the_Seventh_Galaxy "Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy")_, before Connors' replacement by [Al Di Meola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Di_Meola "Al Di Meola"), who later played on _[Where Have I Known You Before](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_Have_I_Known_You_Before "Where Have I Known You Before")_, _[No Mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Mystery "No Mystery")_ and _[Romantic Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_Warrior "Romantic Warrior")_.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-19) In 1976, Corea released _[My Spanish Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Spanish_Heart "My Spanish Heart")_, influenced by Hispanic music and featuring vocalist [Gayle Moran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gayle_Moran "Gayle Moran") (Corea's wife) and violinist [Jean-Luc Ponty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Luc_Ponty "Jean-Luc Ponty"). The album combined jazz and [flamenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamenco "Flamenco"), supported by [Minimoog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimoog "Minimoog") synthesizer and a horn section. He collaborated with flamenco guitarist [Paco De Lucía](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paco_De_Luc%C3%ADa "Paco De Lucía") years later on the _[Touchstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchstone_(album) "Touchstone (album)")_ and _[Zyryab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zyryab "Zyryab")_ albums.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] ### Duet projects \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chick_Corea&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Duet projects")\] [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/SDSC_0010_%286900650522%29.jpg/330px-SDSC_0010_%286900650522%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SDSC_0010_(6900650522).jpg) Corea at a dual- [Gary Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Burton "Gary Burton") concert in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), April 2012 In the 1970s, Corea started working with vibraphonist [Gary Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Burton "Gary Burton"), with whom he recorded several duet albums for ECM, including 1972's _[Crystal Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Silence "Crystal Silence")_. They reunited in 2006 for a concert tour. A new record called _[The New Crystal Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Crystal_Silence "The New Crystal Silence")_ was issued in 2008 and won a Grammy Award in 2009. The package includes a disc of duets and another disc with the [Sydney Symphony Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Symphony_Orchestra "Sydney Symphony Orchestra").\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Towards the end of the 1970s, Corea embarked on a series of concerts with fellow pianist Herbie Hancock. These concerts were presented in elegant settings with both artists dressed formally and performing on concert grand pianos. The two played each other's compositions, as well as pieces by other composers such as [Béla Bartók](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9la_Bart%C3%B3k "Béla Bartók"), and duets. In 1982, Corea performed _The Meeting_, a live duet with the classical pianist [Friedrich Gulda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Gulda "Friedrich Gulda").\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] In December 2007, Corea recorded a duet album, _The Enchantment_, with banjoist [Béla Fleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9la_Fleck "Béla Fleck").[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-20) Fleck and Corea toured extensively for the album in 2007. Fleck was nominated in the Best Instrumental Composition category at the [49th Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/49th_Grammy_Awards "49th Grammy Awards") for the track "Spectacle".[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-21) In 2008, Corea collaborated with Japanese pianist [Hiromi Uehara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiromi_Uehara "Hiromi Uehara") on the live album _Duet (Chick Corea and Hiromi)_. The duo played a concert at Tokyo's [Budokan arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nippon_Budokan "Nippon Budokan") on April 30.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-22) In 2015, Corea reprised the duet concert series with Hancock, again sticking to a dueling-piano format, though both now integrated synthesizers into their repertoire. The first concert in this series was at the [Paramount Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Theatre_(Seattle) "Paramount Theatre (Seattle)") in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle") and included improvisations, compositions by the duo, and standards by other composers.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-23) ### Later work \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chick_Corea&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Later work")\] [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Chickcoreaband_ny.JPG/500px-Chickcoreaband_ny.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chickcoreaband_ny.JPG) The [Chick Corea Elektric Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea_Elektric_Band "Chick Corea Elektric Band") at the [Blue Note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Note_(jazz_clubs) "Blue Note (jazz clubs)") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), 2007 Corea's other bands included the [Chick Corea Elektric Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea_Elektric_Band "Chick Corea Elektric Band"), its trio reduction called "Akoustic Band", Origin, and its trio reduction called the New Trio. Corea signed a record deal with [GRP Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GRP_Records "GRP Records") in 1986 which led to the release of ten albums between 1986 and 1994, seven with the Elektric Band, two with the Akoustic Band, and a solo album, _Expressions_.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] The Akoustic Band released a self-titled album in 1989 and a live follow-up, _Alive_, in 1991, both featuring [John Patitucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Patitucci "John Patitucci") on bass and [Dave Weckl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Weckl "Dave Weckl") on drums. It marked a return to traditional jazz trio instrumentation in Corea's career, and the bulk of his subsequent recordings have featured acoustic piano.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-24) In 1992, Corea started his own label, [Stretch Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stretch_Records "Stretch Records").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-ALLMUSIC-3) In 2001, the Chick Corea New Trio, with bassist [Avishai Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avishai_Cohen_(bassist) "Avishai Cohen (bassist)") and drummer [Jeff Ballard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Ballard_(musician) "Jeff Ballard (musician)"), released the album _[Past, Present & Futures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Past,_Present_&_Futures?action=edit&redlink=1 "Past, Present & Futures (page does not exist)")_. The eleven-song album includes only one standard ( [Fats Waller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fats_Waller "Fats Waller")'s " [Jitterbug Waltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jitterbug_Waltz "Jitterbug Waltz")"). The rest of the tunes are Corea originals. He participated in 1998's _[Like Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like_Minds_(album) "Like Minds (album)")_ with old associates Gary Burton on vibraphone, Dave Holland on bass, Roy Haynes on drums, and [Pat Metheny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Metheny "Pat Metheny") playing guitars.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] During the later part of his career, Corea also explored [contemporary classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_classical_music "Contemporary classical music"). He composed his first [piano concerto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_concerto "Piano concerto")—an adaptation of his signature piece "Spain" for a full symphony orchestra—and performed it in 1999 with the [London Philharmonic Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Philharmonic_Orchestra "London Philharmonic Orchestra"). In 2004, he composed his first work without keyboards: his [String Quartet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_quartet "String quartet") No. 1 was written for the [Orion String Quartet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_String_Quartet "Orion String Quartet") and performed by them at 2004's [Summerfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summerfest "Summerfest") in Wisconsin.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Corea continued recording fusion albums such as _To the Stars_ (2004) and _[The Ultimate Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ultimate_Adventure "The Ultimate Adventure")_ (2006). The latter won the [Grammy Award for Best Jazz Instrumental Album, Individual or Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Jazz_Instrumental_Album,_Individual_or_Group "Grammy Award for Best Jazz Instrumental Album, Individual or Group") for 2007.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-25) In 2008, the third version of Return to Forever (Corea, Stanley Clarke, [Lenny White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenny_White "Lenny White"), and Di Meola) reunited for a worldwide tour. The reunion received positive reviews from jazz and mainstream publications.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-26) Most of the group's studio recordings were re-released on the compilation _Return to Forever: The Anthology_ to coincide with the tour. A concert DVD recorded during their performance at the [Montreux Jazz Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreux_Jazz_Festival "Montreux Jazz Festival") was released in May 2009. He also worked on a [collaboration CD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chick_Corea_Songbook "The Chick Corea Songbook") with the vocal group [The Manhattan Transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Manhattan_Transfer "The Manhattan Transfer").\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Chick_Corea_and_John_McLaughlin%2C_Blue_Note_Jazz_Club%2C_New_York_City%2C_10_December_2016.jpg/250px-Chick_Corea_and_John_McLaughlin%2C_Blue_Note_Jazz_Club%2C_New_York_City%2C_10_December_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chick_Corea_and_John_McLaughlin,_Blue_Note_Jazz_Club,_New_York_City,_10_December_2016.jpg) Corea with [John McLaughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McLaughlin_(musician) "John McLaughlin (musician)") at the NYC Blue Note, 2016 A new group, the [Five Peace Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_Peace_Band "Five Peace Band"), began a world tour in October 2008. The ensemble included John McLaughlin, whom Corea had previously worked with in Miles Davis's late 1960s bands, including the group that recorded Davis's classic album _Bitches Brew_. Joining Corea and McLaughlin were saxophonist [Kenny Garrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Garrett "Kenny Garrett") and bassist [Christian McBride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_McBride "Christian McBride"). Drummer [Vinnie Colaiuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinnie_Colaiuta "Vinnie Colaiuta") played with the band in Europe and on select North American dates; [Brian Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Blade "Brian Blade") played all dates in Asia and Australia, and most dates in North America. The vast reach of Corea's music was celebrated in a 2011 retrospective with Corea guesting with the [Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_at_Lincoln_Center_Orchestra "Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra") in the [Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts"); a _New York Times_ reviewer had high praise for the occasion: "Mr. Corea was masterly with the other musicians, absorbing the rhythm and feeding the soloists. It sounded like a band, and Mr. Corea had no need to dominate; his authority was clear without raising volume."[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-27) A new band, Chick Corea & The Vigil, featured Corea with bassist [Hadrien Feraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadrien_Feraud "Hadrien Feraud"), [Marcus Gilmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Gilmore "Marcus Gilmore") on drums (carrying on from his grandfather, [Roy Haynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Haynes "Roy Haynes")), saxes, flute, and bass clarinet from Origin vet [Tim Garland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Garland "Tim Garland"), and guitarist Charles Altura.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Corea celebrated his 75th birthday in 2016 by playing with more than 20 different groups during a six-week stand at the [Blue Note Jazz Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Note_Jazz_Club "Blue Note Jazz Club") in [Greenwich Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Village "Greenwich Village"), New York City. "I pretty well ignore the numbers that make up 'age'. It seems to be the best way to go. I have always just concentrated on having the most fun I can with the adventure of music."[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-28) ## Personal life \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chick_Corea&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Personal life")\] Corea and his first wife Joanie had two children; the marriage ended in divorce. In 1972, Corea married his second wife, vocalist/pianist [Gayle Moran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gayle_Moran "Gayle Moran").[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-29)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-30) In 1968, Corea read _[Dianetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dianetics:_The_Modern_Science_of_Mental_Health "Dianetics: The Modern Science of Mental Health")_, author [L. Ron Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L._Ron_Hubbard "L. Ron Hubbard")'s well-known self-help book, and developed an interest in Hubbard's other works in the early 1970s: "I came into contact with L. Ron Hubbard's material in 1968 with _Dianetics_ and it kind of opened my mind up and it got me into seeing that my potential for communication was a lot greater than I thought it was."[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-31) Corea said that [Scientology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientology "Scientology") became a profound influence on his musical direction in the early 1970s: "I no longer wanted to satisfy myself. I really want to connect with the world and make my music mean something to people."[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-32) With Clarke[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-ediriwira-33) Corea played on _[Space Jazz: The soundtrack of the book Battlefield Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Jazz "Space Jazz")_, a 1982 album to accompany L. Ron Hubbard's novel [_Battlefield Earth_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battlefield_Earth_(novel) "Battlefield Earth (novel)").[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-34) Corea was excluded from a concert during the [1993 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1993 World Championships in Athletics") in [Stuttgart, Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuttgart,_Germany "Stuttgart, Germany"). The concert's organizers excluded him after the state government of [Baden-Württemberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baden-W%C3%BCrttemberg "Baden-Württemberg") had announced it would review its subsidies for events featuring avowed members of Scientology.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Laut.de-35)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-Scientology_SZ-36) After Corea's complaint against this policy before the administrative court was unsuccessful in 1996,[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-37) members of the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress"), in a letter to the German government, denounced the ban as a violation of Corea's human rights.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-billboard-38) Corea was not banned from performing in Germany, however, and had several appearances at the government-supported [International Jazz Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Jazz_Festivals_Organization "International Jazz Festivals Organization") in [Burghausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burghausen,_Alt%C3%B6tting "Burghausen, Altötting"); he was awarded a plaque on Burghausen's "Street of Fame" in 2011.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Corea#cite_note-ovbonline-39) Corea died at his home in [Tampa, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa,_Florida "Tampa, Florida"), on February 9, 2021, shortly after being diagnosed with a rare form of cancer. He was - bandleader | | Instrument | [Drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_kit "Drum kit") | | Years active | 1961–1997 | Musical artist **Anthony Tillmon Williams** (December 12, 1945 – February 23, 1997)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-1) was an American [jazz drummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_drumming "Jazz drumming"). Williams first gained fame as a member of [Miles Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_Davis "Miles Davis")'s " [Second Great Quintet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_Davis_Quintet#Second_Great_Quintet_(1964%E2%80%9368) "Miles Davis Quintet")", and later pioneered [jazz fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_fusion "Jazz fusion") with Davis's group and his own combo, [The Tony Williams Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tony_Williams_Lifetime "The Tony Williams Lifetime").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-2) In 1970, music critic [Robert Christgau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Christgau "Robert Christgau") described him as "probably the best drummer in the world".[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-3) Williams was inducted into the _[Modern Drummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Drummer "Modern Drummer")_ Hall of Fame in 1986 and the [Percussive Arts Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percussive_Arts_Society "Percussive Arts Society") Hall of Fame in 1997.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-4) ## Life and career Williams was born in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"), and grew up in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-drummerworld-5) He was of African, Portuguese, and Chinese descent.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-drummerworld-5)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-6) He studied with drummer [Alan Dawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Dawson "Alan Dawson") at the age of 11, and began playing professionally at the age of 13 with saxophonist [Sam Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Rivers_(jazz_musician) "Sam Rivers (jazz musician)"). Saxophonist [Jackie McLean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_McLean "Jackie McLean") hired Williams when he, Williams, was 16.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-drummerworld-5)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-7) As a young drummer, he was influenced by [Max Roach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Roach "Max Roach"), [Art Blakey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Blakey "Art Blakey"), [Philly Joe Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philly_Joe_Jones "Philly Joe Jones"), [Roy Haynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Haynes "Roy Haynes"), [Louis Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Hayes "Louis Hayes"), and [Jimmy Cobb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Cobb "Jimmy Cobb").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-10) At 17, Williams joined [Miles Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_Davis "Miles Davis") in what was later dubbed Davis's [Second Great Quintet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_Davis_Quintet#Second_Great_Quintet_(1964%E2%80%9368) "Miles Davis Quintet")—with saxophonist [Wayne Shorter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Shorter "Wayne Shorter"), pianist [Herbie Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Hancock "Herbie Hancock"), and bassist [Ron Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Carter "Ron Carter"). Davis had been in something of a creative lull, and critics noted the young Tony Williams' playing spurred the others on.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-fordham-11) Williams was a vital element of the group, called by Davis in his autobiography "the center that the group's sound revolved around".[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-12) His playing helped redefine the role of the jazz [rhythm section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_section "Rhythm section") through the use of [polyrhythms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyrhythm "Polyrhythm") and [metric modulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_modulation "Metric modulation"). Meanwhile, he recorded his first two albums as a leader for the [Blue Note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Note_Records "Blue Note Records") label: _[Life Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_Time_(Tony_Williams_album) "Life Time (Tony Williams album)")_ (1964) and _[Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_(Tony_Williams_album) "Spring (Tony Williams album)")_ (1965). He also recorded as a sideman for the label including the classics _[Out to Lunch!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Out_to_Lunch! "Out to Lunch!")_ with [Eric Dolphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Dolphy "Eric Dolphy") and _[Point of Departure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_of_Departure_(Andrew_Hill_album) "Point of Departure (Andrew Hill album)")_ with [Andrew Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Hill_(pianist) "Andrew Hill (pianist)"), both in 1964. In 1969 Williams formed [The Tony Williams Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tony_Williams_Lifetime "The Tony Williams Lifetime"), with [John McLaughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McLaughlin_(musician) "John McLaughlin (musician)") on guitar and [Larry Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Young_(musician) "Larry Young (musician)") on organ.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-drummerworld-5) Lifetime was a pioneering band of the [fusion movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz-rock_fusion "Jazz-rock fusion").[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-LarkinJazz-13) Their first album was [_Emergency!_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency!_(album) "Emergency! (album)"). For the album _[Turn It Over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn_It_Over "Turn It Over")_, the trio was joined by bass guitarist and vocalist [Jack Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Bruce "Jack Bruce"). After several more releases and touring, Lifetime disbanded. In 1975, Williams formed "The New Tony Williams Lifetime", featuring bassist [Tony Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Newton_(American_musician) "Tony Newton (American musician)"), keyboardist [Alan Pasqua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Pasqua "Alan Pasqua") and guitarist [Allan Holdsworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allan_Holdsworth "Allan Holdsworth"), who recorded two albums for [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"): _[Believe It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believe_It_(album) "Believe It (album)")_ and _[Million Dollar Legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million_Dollar_Legs_(album) "Million Dollar Legs (album)")_. In 1976, Williams reunited with his colleagues from the Miles Davis Quintet.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-drummerworld-5) (Davis himself was in the midst of a six-year hiatus and was "replaced" by trumpeter [Freddie Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Hubbard "Freddie Hubbard").) [\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-drummerworld-5) A record of their concert was later released as _[V.S.O.P.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VSOP_(album) "VSOP (album)")_ ("Very Special One-time Performance"), the name under which the group toured and recorded for several years.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-drummerworld-5)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-14) [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Tony_Williams1.jpg/500px-Tony_Williams1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tony_Williams1.jpg) Williams in [Half Moon Bay, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_Moon_Bay,_California "Half Moon Bay, California"), 1986 In 1979, Williams, McLaughlin, and bassist [Jaco Pastorius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaco_Pastorius "Jaco Pastorius") united for a performance at the [Havana Jazz Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festivals_in_Havana#Havana_International_Jazz_Festival "Festivals in Havana").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-drummerworld-5) This trio came to be known as the [Trio of Doom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trio_of_Doom "Trio of Doom"), and a recording of their performance (along with some studio tracks recorded in New York shortly thereafter) was released in 2007. Williams and Pastorius also played together on "Good Question" from the 1978 Herbie Hancock album _[Sunlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunlight_(Herbie_Hancock_album) "Sunlight (Herbie Hancock album)")_. Williams appears with the group [Fuse One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuse_One "Fuse One") on their 1980 album.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-ALLMUSIC-15) In 1985, Williams returned to Blue Note with the album _Foreign Intrigue_. Eventually Williams formed his own acoustic quintet with trumpeter [Wallace Roney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallace_Roney "Wallace Roney"), saxophonist [Bill Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Pierce_(saxophonist) "Bill Pierce (saxophonist)"), pianist [Mulgrew Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mulgrew_Miller "Mulgrew Miller") and bassist [Ira Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ira_Coleman "Ira Coleman").[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-LarkinJazz-13) The quintet played Williams' compositions almost exclusively, recording and touring extensively from 1986 to 1992, culminating in the album _[The Story of Neptune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_of_Neptune "The Story of Neptune")_. Williams guested with the band [Public Image Ltd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Image_Ltd "Public Image Ltd"), fronted by [John Lydon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lydon "John Lydon"), on their release titled _[Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album_(Public_Image_Ltd_album) "Album (Public Image Ltd album)")_ (1986). On February 20, 1997, Williams checked into [Seton Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Medical_Center "Seton Medical Center") in [Daly City, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_City,_California "Daly City, California"), suffering from stomach pain. Three days later, while recuperating from [gallbladder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallbladder "Gallbladder") surgery, he died of a [heart attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myocardial_infarction "Myocardial infarction"). He was 51 years old.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-nytimes_1997-16)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-latimes_1997-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-19) ## Personal life Williams lived and taught in the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") until his death in 1997.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-latimes_1997-18)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-nytimes_1997-16) One of his final recordings was _[The Last Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Wave_(album) "The Last Wave (album)")_ by the trio known as [Arcana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcana_(American_band) "Arcana (American band)"), a release organized by [Bill Laswell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Laswell "Bill Laswell").[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Williams_(drummer)#cite_note-20) ## Discography ### As leader/co-leader | Recording date | Title | Label | Year released | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1964-08 | _[Life Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_Time_(Tony_Williams_album) "Life Time (Tony Williams album)")_ | [Blue Note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Note_Records "Blue Note Records") | 1965 | | | 1965-08 | _[Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_(Tony_Williams_album) "Spring (Tony Williams album)")_ | Blue Note | 1966 | | | 1969-05 | _[Emergency!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency!_(album) "Emergency!
